fields.title: Routing and choosing a model for the task
fields.keyTakeaway: Simple feature steps are executed by cheap models without quality loss, and this is verified with evals — going from strong model to weak model, not the other way around.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Is it mandatory to use a single model for the entire feature?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Using the strongest model for everything is a simple solution that costs several times more than necessary. Splitting by task complexity usually yields manifold savings without losing quality.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Different steps of the same feature have different complexity. Question classification, query rewriting, field extraction are simple tasks that small models handle well. Final answer generation is complex.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **[[routing|Routing]]** is choosing a model for a request. Two types:
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Static.* Each step always runs on its own model. Simple, predictable. *Dynamic.* A model or classifier decides which request is complex and routes it accordingly. More economical, harder to operate, requires deciding what to do in case of incorrect classification.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: Product requirement for dynamic routing: **degradation must be in favor of quality.** Incorrectly routing a complex request to a weak model is worse than the opposite.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **[[distillation|Distillation]].** Training a small model to replicate a large model's behavior on your task. Requires volume and work, justified at large volumes of identical requests.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **[[quantization|Quantization]].** Reducing weight precision for the sake of speed and memory. Pertains to self-hosting models, covered in `AI3`.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Practical rule for getting started: **start with a strong model, measure quality, then try a weaker one and see where quality drops.** The reverse order leads to unsatisfactory quality where it's unclear whether the model or the prompt is at fault.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The "ask about a product" feature after splitting:
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Before splitting, all steps ran on a medium model at a cost of 3.4 kopecks. Afterward — 2.1. Quality according to evals did not change.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: We separately tested whether a small model could handle answer generation. Evals showed a 14% drop in factual precision — too much. We kept the medium one.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Classification on a small model produced an unexpected side effect: medical questions started getting filtered out before the main call, meaning cheaper and more reliably than through an instruction rule.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Routing complicates the system and debugging: when an answer is bad, you need to figure out at which step and on which model. It is justified at noticeable volumes.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Simple feature steps are executed by cheap models without quality loss, and this is verified with evals — going from strong model to weak model, not the other way around.
